title: U.S. House · Montana's 1st District
area: Western Montana, including Missoula, Kalispell and Flathead County.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Rep. Ryan Zinke (R) did not run for re-election. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee named Sam Forstag to its "Red to Blue" program and the National Republican Congressional Committee named Aaron Flint to its "MAGA Majority" program, reflecting the district's ticket-splitting history: in 2024 Donald Trump carried the district 54%-43% while Zinke won it by a smaller 52%-45% margin and Democratic Sen. Jon Tester won it 50%-49%. As of July 21, 2026, Cook Political Report, DDHQ/The Hill, Inside Elections and Sabato's Crystal Ball rated the general election Likely Republican.

candidates.name: Aaron Flint
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary on June 2, 2026.

summary.text: Aaron Flint is the Republican nominee for Montana's open 1st Congressional District seat. He is a longtime radio talk show host and Army National Guard and Reserve veteran who earlier worked for U.S. Sen. Conrad Burns and later as a state director for Republican officeholders, and this is his first run for office. He won the June 2 Republican primary with 50.1% of the vote.

background.text: Is the grandson of newspaper publishers in Glasgow, Montana, according to Montana Free Press, and lived in Billings for many years before moving with his family to Kalispell in the summer of 2025.
Attended Howard University in Washington, D.C., before enrolling at the University of Montana in spring 2002 and joining ROTC and the Montana National Guard.

Began his political career in the late 1990s working in the Washington, D.C. office of Sen. Conrad Burns, answering phones and constituent mail, and later became Burns's legislative aide for energy policy.
Served in the U.S. Army National Guard and Reserves from 2002 to 2024, with deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan; Montana Free Press reports he was awarded two Bronze Stars.
Worked as state director for then-Rep. Greg Gianforte (per Montana Free Press) and for Rep. Ryan Zinke (per Ballotpedia), and was communications director for Gianforte's 2016 gubernatorial campaign.

Hosts the statewide morning radio program "Montana Talks," broadcast from KBUL in Billings, and has worked in local television and radio journalism for about 25 years, according to Montana Free Press.
Entered the race after Rep. Ryan Zinke announced in March 2026 that he would not seek re-election; Zinke and President Donald Trump endorsed Flint, who is a first-time candidate.

priorities.text: "I have heard firsthand their frustrations with government and what they believe needs to change. That has given me a different perspective than most candidates. I am not guessing what people want; I have been listening to them for nearly two decades."

positions.summary: In an October 2026 Montana Free Press questionnaire, says Border Patrol and ICE should have the personnel and equipment to deport illegal immigrants from Montana, starting with those convicted of violent crimes and drug trafficking.
positions.quote: That means giving Border Patrol and ICE the personnel and equipment to secure our borders, including our northern border, and deport illegal immigrants from Montana, starting with those convicted of violent crimes and drug trafficking.

candidates.researchNotes: Basic-tier research from Ballotpedia, the Montana Free Press March 2026 questionnaire and October 2026 immigration feature, and his campaign website issues page. No statements found on abortion, guns, taxes on high earners, or minimum wage.

statements.quote: We also need to make it easier to build homes and businesses in our state.
I would not support anything that ties the hands of our military or prevents the President from acting quickly when American lives are at risk.
statements.context: In a March 2026 Montana Free Press questionnaire, in answer to whether the War Powers Resolution should be enforced

candidates.name: Sam Forstag
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary on June 2, 2026 over Ryan Busse, Russell Cleveland and Matt Rains; named to the DCCC's "Red to Blue" program.

summary.text: Sam Forstag is the Democratic nominee for Montana's open 1st Congressional District seat. A Missoula smokejumper with the U.S. Forest Service and union local vice president, he previously did policy and lobbying work in the Montana Legislature and was student body president at the University of Montana. He won the June 2 Democratic primary with 37.4% of the vote and describes himself as a "working Montanan."

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, was raised by a mother who worked extra nursing shifts and a father who relied on food stamps while earning a teaching certificate to become a public school teacher.

Graduated from the University of Montana, where he was a student senator with the Associated Students of the University of Montana (ASUM) and was elected ASUM president his senior year; says he worked his way through school.

Worked for two years at Central House Strategies doing policy and lobbying work during the Montana Legislature, and, per his LinkedIn profile as cited by the Daily Montanan, helped build and run the Montana Coalition to Solve Homelessness.
Has worked for the U.S. Forest Service for several years, including as a smokejumper, a wildland firefighter who parachutes into remote areas to fight fires.

Serves as vice president of National Federation of Federal Employees (NFFE) Local 60, which the Daily Montanan reports represents roughly 800 Forest Service workers on the Lolo, Bitterroot and Custer-Gallatin National Forests.
Had not run for political office outside the University of Montana before this campaign and announced his candidacy on Jan. 5, 2026.

priorities.text: Describes himself as "a smokejumper, union leader, and working Montanan running for Congress in MT-01."

In his Candidate Connection survey, says he knows what it is like to worry about a parent working too much, to rely on food stamps, and to work multiple jobs while attending school and still fall short on rent.

positions.summary: Calls for letting everyone buy into Medicare and for restoring and expanding enhanced ACA subsidies.
positions.quote: Restore and expand the enhanced ACA subsidies to ensure access to free health coverage for anyone making $70,000 or less and affordable healthcare for everyone.

positions.summary: Calls for raising the corporate income tax rate to 35%, a 30% minimum tax rate on income over $1 million, and a 5% tax on fortunes over $1 billion.
positions.quote: Make corporations carry their own weight by raising the corporate income tax rate to 35%.

positions.summary: Says he would protect access to abortion by codifying Roe v. Wade.
positions.quote: Protect access to abortion and reproductive health by codifying Roe v. Wade

positions.summary: Calls for raising the federal minimum wage to at least $15 per hour and indexing it to inflation.
positions.quote: Raise the federal minimum wage to at least $15 per hour and fix it permanently by tying it to the rate of inflation.

positions.summary: Calls for federal incentives for zoning and regulatory reform where restrictions block housing, alongside affordable-housing investment.
positions.quote: Incentivize zoning and regulatory reform in places where onerous and outdated zoning restrictions are standing in the way of building housing where working people need it most.

positions.summary: In a March 2026 questionnaire, said Congress should act under the War Powers Resolution and Article I and vote to end the war with Iran.
positions.quote: Congress should do their job as outlined in the War Powers Resolution and Article I of the U.S. Constitution

positions.summary: Says tariffs can be a responsible tool in targeted uses, but calls recent tariff policy reckless and destructive and says tariffs should not be used to punish allies.
positions.quote: what we’ve seen over the past couple years has been a reckless, destructive tariff policy that’s hurt Montana farmers and ranchers

candidates.researchNotes: Basic-tier research from Ballotpedia; campaign website reviewed only via Ballotpedia's quoted excerpt. Positions added October 2026 from the Montana Free Press March 2026 questionnaire and the candidate's campaign site.

candidates.name: Nick Sheedy
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed after the Libertarian primary was canceled.

summary.text: Nick Sheedy is the Libertarian Party nominee for Montana's open 1st Congressional District seat. He advanced to the general election after the June 2 Libertarian primary, in which he received 1,202 votes as the only candidate. Little public biographical information about him was found.

background.text: Became the Libertarian nominee for Montana's 1st Congressional District in the June 2, 2026 primary, in which he was the only candidate on the Libertarian ballot.

In a March 2026 Montana Free Press candidate questionnaire, said he would support strengthening the War Powers Resolution, ending the Federal Reserve, and federal legislation limiting campaign contributions to people eligible to vote.

priorities.text: Says the best thing federal officeholders can do on home ownership and cost of living is monetary reform, including ending the Federal Reserve.
priorities.quote: We should end the Federal Reserve and the federal banking cartel that has destroyed the value of the US Dollar with continual inflationary policies, money-supply controls and interest rate manipulation.

priorities.text: Wants federal legislation limiting campaign contributions to people eligible to vote, nullifying the Citizens United decision.
priorities.quote: I would also like to see federal legislation pass that nullifies the Supreme Court's 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission by limiting all financial contributions to political campaigns and committees to persons who are eligible to vote in the United States.

priorities.text: Wants to lower the regulatory burden he says restricts the supply of healthcare providers.
priorities.quote: I believe that the best way for Congress to improve access to healthcare generally would be to lower the regulatory burden, which artificially restricts the supply of healthcare providers.

positions.summary: In a March 2026 Montana Free Press questionnaire, says the War Powers Resolution should be strengthened so a president cannot engage in war without a congressional declaration.
positions.quote: The War Powers Resolution of 1973 should be strengthened so that the President cannot engage in war without Congress declaring war, as prescribed by the US Constitution.

candidates.researchNotes: Basic-tier research from his March 2026 Montana Free Press written questionnaire (four answers). No campaign website or Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey found; he did not respond to MTFP's October immigration, healthcare or affordability questions.

statements.quote: While federal laws and policies should not hinder healthcare services to rural areas, I am not sure the federal government has or should have a significant role to play when it comes to local hospitals and clinics
statements.context: In a March 2026 Montana Free Press questionnaire
